title: Modern cell-based assays for biomedical research: from conventional methods to AI-driven high content analysis.
authors: Venkataramaiah C
abstract: In vitro cell-based assays are fundamental tools in biomedical research, supporting investigations of cellular physiology, disease mechanisms, drug discovery, toxicology, regenerative medicine, and precision therapeutics. However, conventional two-dimensional (2D) cell culture models often fail to recapitulate the structural complexity and physiological functions of native tissues, prompting the development of advanced platforms, including three-dimensional (3D) cultures, organoids, organ-on-a-chip technologies, and microphysiological systems. Recent advances in cell viability and cytotoxicity assessment, functional cellular analysis, molecular profiling, clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based functional genomics, high-content imaging, flow cytometry, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and automated high-throughput screening have expanded the analytical capabilities of cell-based assays. Furthermore, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image analysis and computational biology has enhanced cellular phenotyping, biomarker discovery, and mechanistic investigation, with the potential to improve the prediction of therapeutic efficacy and toxicity. Nevertheless, challenges related to physiological relevance, technical variability, inadequate standardization, high operational costs, scalability, poor reproducibility, cell-line misidentification, batch-to-batch variation, and inconsistent reporting continue to hinder translational applications. Future progress will depend on integrating physiologically relevant models with AI-driven analytics, spatial multi-omics, digital pathology, automated screening, and microphysiological systems. Standardized protocols, harmonized reporting practices, and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to improve reproducibility, strengthen regulatory acceptance, advance precision medicine, and reduce reliance on animal experimentation. In this context, this review critically evaluates conventional and emerging in vitro cell-based assays, emphasizing their biological principles, analytical capabilities, translational applications, and practical limitations, while highlighting future opportunities to improve predictive accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical translation.

title: Next-generation anti-obesity drugs: emerging molecular targets and translational opportunities.
authors: Shetty S, Rangle A, Mukherjee AG, Bharti AK, Jena SP, Prince SE, Gopalakrishnan AV
journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
abstract: PURPOSE: Obesity is a heterogeneous, chronic metabolic disease driven by dysregulation of energy homeostasis across interconnected central nervous system, gastrointestinal, adipose, endocrine, immune, and mitochondrial networks. Despite the established roles of lifestyle intervention and metabolic/bariatric surgery, limitations in accessibility, durability, and interindividual response have stimulated the development of mechanism-based pharmacotherapies. This review critically examines emerging therapeutic strategies targeting integrated energy-regulatory pathways and evaluates their translational potential for precision obesity management. METHODS: Current evidence was synthesized across major biological systems governing appetite, energy expenditure, and metabolic adaptation. Central melanocortin, Neuropeptide Y (NPY)/ Agouti-related peptide (AgRP), serotonergic, dopaminergic, and endocannabinoid pathways were considered alongside gut-derived incretin, amylin, Peptide YY (PYY), ghrelin, Fibroblast Growth Factor (FGF), and bile acid signaling. Emerging approaches targeting adipose remodeling, thermogenesis, mitochondrial energetics, AMPK-mTOR-sirtuin signaling, inflammation, and fibrosis were also evaluated. Genetic, epigenetic, and artificial intelligence-based approaches to patient stratification were incorporated to assess prospects for precision therapy. RESULTS: Obesity pharmacotherapy is shifting from conventional appetite suppression toward coordinated modulation of interconnected metabolic pathways. Incretin-based and multi-agonist therapies provide the strongest clinical evidence for substantial weight reduction and metabolic improvement. However, treatment discontinuation, weight regain, adverse effects, cost, and heterogeneous therapeutic responses remain major challenges. Strategies targeting adipose tissue dysfunction, mitochondrial metabolism, thermogenesis, immune-metabolic signaling, and fibrosis offer additional opportunities for disease modification, although many remain in preclinical or early clinical development. Increasing evidence for biological heterogeneity supports individualized therapeutic selection. CONCLUSION: The emerging therapeutic paradigm positions obesity as a systems-level disorder requiring mechanism-informed, individualized intervention. Integrating CNS-gut-adipose-mitochondrial biology with multi-omics, biomarkers, and artificial intelligence may enable more durable and precise treatment. Long-term safety, durability, affordability, equitable access, and clinical validation remain essential for translation.

title: Next-generation hyphenated analytical technologies in natural product research: From high-resolution separation and structural elucidation to dereplication, metabolomics and drug discovery.
authors: Dar AA, Mukhtar M, Shameem SA, Singh N
abstract: Natural products occupy a unique position at the interface of chemistry, biology and medicine and continue to provide structurally diverse molecules for drug discovery, chemical biology, nutrition and therapeutic development. Their investigation, however, is complicated by the enormous chemical complexity of natural-product extracts, the presence of structurally related metabolites, isomeric and isobaric compounds, wide concentration ranges, matrix effects and the frequent occurrence of previously uncharacterized constituents. Over the past decade, advances in chromatographic separation, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS), ion mobility spectrometry (IMS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and computational analysis have fundamentally changed how these challenges are addressed. High performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS), HPLC-MS/MS, HPLC-NMR, LC-solid-phase extraction (SPE)-NMR and capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry (CE-MS) have evolved from individual hyphenated techniques into integrated analytical workflows capable of linking chemical separation with molecular characterization, dereplication and biological prioritization. In parallel, molecular networking, spectral databases, in silico fragmentation, machine learning and metabolomics platforms have transformed the interpretation of increasingly complex datasets. This review critically examines these developments, emphasizing the complementary information generated by chromatographic, MS and NMR measurements and their integration with computational approaches. Particular attention is given to HRMS/MS, data-independent acquisition, ion mobility, LC-SPE-NMR, molecular networking, spectral-library searching, metabolite annotation confidence and emerging artificial-intelligence-assisted workflows. The review argues that the principal transformation in natural-product analysis is not simply improved instrumental sensitivity, but the emergence of multidimensional and computationally integrated workflows that connect extraction, separation, detection, structural annotation, dereplication, metabolomics and bioactivity-guided discovery. Remaining challenges including incomplete databases, isomer discrimination, annotation uncertainty, reproducibility and the need for orthogonal structure confirmation are discussed, together with future opportunities for automated, multidimensional and FAIR-data-enabled natural-product discovery.

title: Bioactive gas-eluting biomaterial platforms: gaseous medicine strategy for peripheral nerve injury.
authors: Sun M, Qin L, Fan X, Luo Y, Li S, Wang H, Shi H, Yu M
abstract: A rapidly growing body of evidence suggests that medical gases and gasotransmitters are potent bioinstructive effectors that can remodel the regenerative niche of peripheral nerve injury and promote peripheral nerve regeneration. This review provides an integrative synthesis of contemporary advances in gas-based therapeutics and gas-releasing scaffold platforms, breaking down the mechanistic foundations and translational trajectories. Five cardinal bioactive gases, the medical gases hydrogen and oxygen/ozone, and the gasotransmitters hydrogen sulfide, nitric oxide, and carbon monoxide, collectively orchestrate redox equilibrium, inflammatory cascades, mitochondrial homeostasis, angiogenic activation, and cytoprotective programs. These bioactive gases exert multitargeted actions on neurons, Schwann cells, macrophages, and endothelial cells to coordinate axonal regeneration and tissue-level restoration. However, their clinical deployment is severely limited by rapid diffusion, short biological half-lives, and insufficient sustained bioavailability within the injury site. To overcome these limitations, engineered scaffolds, including nerve guidance conduits, hydrogels, and composite constructs, have been designed for spatially confined, precise gas delivery. Stimuli-responsive platforms operating via reactive oxygen species, pH, photo, or magneto-triggered mechanisms further confer spatiotemporal control over gas liberation, substantially heightening therapeutic specificity. Although considerable preclinical milestones have been achieved, persistent barriers, including heterogeneous delivery strategies, the absence of standardized dosing paradigms, insufficient long-term safety validation, and a pronounced deficit of clinical translation, continue to impede progress.

title: Super-speciality medicine in India: A critical review of growth referral gaps and cluster-based reform.
authors: Ghosh K
abstract: Super-speciality medical education in India has expanded rapidly over the past four decades, increasing from fewer than 100 seats in the 1980s to more than 5000 DM/MCh/DrNB seats by 2025. This growth reflects advances in diagnostics and surgical technology, as well as the rising burden of complex non-communicable diseases. Up to 45-58% of tertiary visits involve conditions manageable at primary levels, while rural regions face severe shortages of super-specialists, with 80-85% of specialists concentrated in urban districts. Private multispeciality hospitals host most high-skilled professionals, reinforcing geographic and sectoral inequities. Training quality also varies widely due to faculty shortages, commercialisation, and inconsistent regulatory enforcement. Emerging disciplines such as genomics, metabolic medicine, and precision medicine remain poorly integrated within siloed DM/MCh structures. This critical narrative review synthesised peer-reviewed literature, regulatory documents and national datasets published between 1980 and 2025, identified through a structured search and analysed using the World Health Organization (WHO) health system building blocks framework. The review argues for restructuring India's medical education and service delivery architecture by strengthening general practice, enforcing referral pathways, and standardising training quality. A cluster-based model linking primary care, secondary hubs, and tertiary precision centres is proposed, with reform pathways organised across all six building blocks, to align super-speciality expertise with population needs. Because the evidence relies heavily on a small number of apex institutions and states and on grey literature, the findings should be interpreted with caution.

abstract: Fractionated laser resurfacing for cutaneous rejuvenation delivers tightly controlled columns of thermal injury while preserving intervening tissue for rapid re-epithelialization. Compared to ablative lasers, fractionated lasers have decreased postoperative recovery, prolonged erythema, risk of pigmentary changes, and scarring. This article will focus on the basic principles of fractioned lasers, skin anatomy with relation to laser resurfacing, types of lasers, preoperative, perioperative and postoperative management, and mitigating and treating complications.

title: Gegen qinlian decoction alleviates DSS-induced colitis through modulation of intestinal stem cell homeostasis and M1 macrophage polarization.
authors: Wang M, Yang X, Ji N, Wang X, Cheng Y, Liu Z, Ren L, Leng Z
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) imposes a significant burden on human health and socioeconomic systems. Gegen Qinlian Decoction (GQD) is an effective formula clinically used for the treatment of IBD. However, the underlying mechanisms of GQD in treating colitis remain incompletely elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of GQD in DSS-induced colitis mice, and explore the underlying mechanisms, thereby providing novel perspectives and strategies for colitis treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A mouse colitis model was induced by administering 2.5% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) in drinking water. The therapeutic efficacy of GQD was assessed by monitoring body weight, disease activity index (DAI), colon length, histopathological damage, inflammatory cytokines, and intestinal mechanical and mucus barrier function. RNA sequencing was performed to reveal the underlying mechanisms. The effects of GQD on macrophage polarization and intestinal stem cells (ISCs) restoration were subsequently examined. RESULTS: GQD treatment significantly alleviated DSS-induced colitis and tissue damage, accompanied by restoration of tight junction protein expression and improvement of mucus barrier function. RNA sequencing suggested that the effects of GQD in colitis mice were closely associated with ISCs and macrophage functions. Experimental validation demonstrated that GQD treatment was associated with increased expression of ISC-associated markers, including AXIN2, and improved goblet cell-associated mucus barrier parameters. Meanwhile, GQD treatment attenuated M1 macrophage polarization, accompanied by decreased inflammatory cytokine levels and alleviation of intestinal inflammation. These effects were also accompanied by reduced SNX10 expression and alterations in Wnt/β-catenin and NLRP3/caspase-1 signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: GQD ameliorates intestinal mucosal barrier function and promotes mucosal healing in DSS-induced colitis mice. These effects are associated with the upregulation of ISC-related markers expression and the inhibition of M1 macrophage polarization.

title: Genetically engineered extracellular vesicles with chimeric antigen receptors of human stem cell-derived neutrophils targeting fibroblast activation protein to modulate tumor microenvironment.
authors: Esmonde C, Sun L, Jin G, Michaelides L, Syed F, Bhattarai J, Driscoll T, Quiñones-Hinojosa A
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most commonly occurring central nervous system tumor, accounting for over 50% of gliomas, with a poor survival rate. A primary driver of GBM progression is the fibrotic stroma, where excess extracellular matrix deposition creates a dense network that excludes immune cells and chemotherapeutic agents. While targeting tumor-associated fibroblasts (TAFs) via fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cells is a promising strategy, off-target toxicities limit the clinical utility of the treatment. To address these safety concerns, extracellular vesicles (EVs) of FAP-CAR-engineered neutrophils differentiated from human pluripotent stem cells were isolated and characterized, including proteomic profile, microRNA content, in vitro bioactivity, and in vivo biodistribution in this study. Multi-omic profiling revealed that CAR engineering enriched EVs with proinflammatory proteins, iron-transferring proteins, and proliferation regulators, and a significant upregulation of miRNAs targeting FAP and proliferation-regulating genes was observed. Functional in vitro assays demonstrated that these EVs are selectively cytotoxic to TAFs, reducing the expression of BCL-2 and RAS-MAPK-ERK signaling pathway genes. These EVs also demonstrated cytotoxicity to patient-derived GBM spheroids. Furthermore, in vivo biodistribution results confirmed that FAP-CAR EVs are capable of systemic circulation and payload delivery, showing a significant increase in accumulation within the liver and spleen compared to free Cy5.5. These findings suggest that CAR engineering enhances the ability of FAP-CAR EVs to inhibit TAF proliferation and induce apoptosis. FAP-targeting CAR EVs are positioned as a targeted bioengineered delivery platform with the potential for remodeling the tumor microenvironment and slowing the progression of desmoplasia in GBM.

title: Sustained delivery of 3D-bioprinted stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles promotes neural regeneration following traumatic brain injury via the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 axis.
authors: Ai Y, Zhang Q, Chen T, Lin L, Chen Z, Liu G, Liu J, Dong Z
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical translation of stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) for traumatic brain injury (TBI) is restricted by low yield in 2D culture and rapid in vivo clearance. OBJECTIVE: To develop an in situ sustained delivery system (3D-sEVs@Gel) encapsulating 3D-bioprinted adipose stem cell (ADSC)-derived sEVs (3D-ADSC-sEVs) within GelMA (Gelatin methacryloyl) hydrogel for long-term functional repair after TBI. METHODS: SEVs derived from coaxially bioprinted 3D-ADSCs were isolated, and a GelMA hydrogel-based delivery system was subsequently constructed. Following orthotopic transplantation of the 3D-sEVs@Gel system into the lesion site after TBI, functional recovery, neural stem cell (NSC) proliferation and lineage-associated responses, and the underlying molecular mechanisms were systematically evaluated through behavioral tests, immunofluorescence, multi-omics, and pharmacological inhibition. RESULTS: SEVs generated using the coaxial alginate-microfiber culture system exhibited an approximately eightfold higher yields and protein loading compared with those obtained from 2D culture. In vivo, 3D-sEVs@Gel prolonged local retention, reduced tissue loss, and significantly improved long-term sensorimotor coordination and spatial memory following TBI. In addition, treatment increased the numbers of proliferating cells co-expressing neural progenitor-, neuronal-, and oligodendroglial-lineage-associated markers within the examined neurogenic regions. Mechanistically, 3D-sEV treatment increased nuclear CREB1 levels in NSCs, promoting PGC-1α transcription and subsequent FNDC5 expression, thereby supporting endogenous neurogenesis and functional neural repair. CONCLUSION: The 3D-sEVs@Gel system promotes chronic neurological reconstruction post-TBI by modulating NSC proliferation and neural lineage-associated responses through the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 pathway, offering a promising cell-free strategy for neural repair and tissue engineering.

title: Two organs, one storm: CNS and hepatic HLH.
authors: Diamond T, McCuaig S, Gorman MP, Henderson LA
abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) often presents as a systemic cytokine storm with multiorgan system involvement; however, single-organ manifestations in the central nervous system (CNS) and liver can dominate the initial presentation. In some circumstances, HLH can exclusively involve the CNS. These organ-predominant presentations are underrecognized and lead to diagnostic uncertainty and treatment delay. Therefore, the purpose of this review is to highlight CNS and liver-predominant presentations of HLH with a focus on clinical features, diagnostic evaluation, differential diagnoses, pathophysiologic mechanisms, and organ-specific treatment considerations. Severe CNS-isolated disease and acute liver failure in children under 2 years of age occurs more frequently in primary versus secondary HLH, where there is an underlying genetic etiology and treatment with hematopoietic stem cell transplant may be curative. Thus, early recognition is critical to facilitate genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis and prompt treatment with immunomodulation to prevent organ damage and death.

title: A portable smartphone-integrated chiral molecularly imprinted electrochemical sensing platform based on L-histidine-functionalized Q-HKUST/PEDOT for highly selective detection of L-tyrosine.
authors: Yu J, Zhang X, Han S, Wang Y, Chu H, Zong W, Leng Q
abstract: l-tyrosine (L-Tyr) is an important amino acid closely associated with human metabolism and neurophysiological functions. Abnormal L-Tyr levels are related to multiple physiological disorders, so accurate detection of L-Tyr in food is of great practical value. This study proposes a novel molecularly imprinted electrochemical sensor (MIP/PEDOT/Q-HKUST-His/SPCE) based on poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) and l-histidine (L-His)-grafted metal-organic framework (Q-HKUST-His) for the detection of L-Tyr. Q-HKUST-His with chiral centers and the conductive polymer PEDOT were sequentially modified on the surface of a screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE) to accelerate electron transfer, increase the effective surface area of the electrode, and facilitate the electropolymerization of molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs). The electrosynthesized MIPs significantly improved the selective recognition and enrichment of L-Tyr. The constructed MIP/PEDOT/Q-HKUST-His/SPCE (MPS) sensor exhibited a wide linear range (0.001-200 μmol L-1) and a low detection limit (0.116 nmol L-1). It also showed excellent selectivity for L-Tyr, with recovery rates of 98.64-104.62%. When coupled with a portable electrochemical workstation and smartphone-based data acquisition system, the proposed sensor enabled sensitive, accurate, and rapid on-site detection of L-Tyr in various food samples.

title: A genetic engineering toolkit for the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii.
authors: Dong H, Xiao C, Zhang Y
abstract: Saccharomyces boulardii (S. boulardii) is the only yeast probiotic widely used in clinical practice and consumer products. It combines gastrointestinal robustness, intrinsic antibiotic tolerance and eukaryotic protein-processing capacity, making it an attractive chassis for engineered probiotics, in situ biomanufacturing and live biotherapeutic delivery. However, host-specific characterization of regulatory elements, candidate genomic integration sites, and multicopy integration strategies remains limited in the clinically used S. boulardii CNCM I-745 background. Here, using S. boulardii CNCM I-745 as the host, we developed and characterized a genetic engineering toolkit that integrates transcriptional control elements with genome-integration strategies. We first quantified the activities of 20 endogenous constitutive promoters, two inducible promoters and six terminators. We then established a markerless CRISPR-Cas9 workflow and evaluated 10 chromosomal integration loci; six of which showed Editing efficiency above 80% while supporting comparable transgene expression without detectable growth penalties. Finally, we constructed an rDNA-repeat-based multicopy integration system that increased transgene expression by 9.8- to 22.6-fold relative to single-copy integration and revealed a significant positive but non-proportional association between estimated copy number and reporter output. Together, this toolkit provides S. boulardii with a set of tunable promoters and terminators, candidate chromosomal integration sites compatible with a markerless CRISPR-Cas9 workflow. These resources expand the genetic accessibility of this probiotic yeast and provide a foundation for developing engineered S. boulardii strains with enhanced probiotic, therapeutic and biomanufacturing functions.

title: Unlocking genetic accessibility in Halomonas bluephagenesis: A high-efficiency transformation chassis enables linear DNA-mediated genome editing.
authors: Xu T, Guo F, Xiang H, Han J
abstract: Halomonas bluephagenesis has emerged as a promising chassis for industrial biotechnology distinguished by its halophilic robustness and capacity for open and continuous fermentation. However, its poor transformability has substantially limited rapid, iterative, and automatable strain engineering. Here, we develop a "restriction release" strategy that increases transformation efficiency from approximately 102 to 107 cfu/μg DNA, rivaling the efficiency of standard laboratory Escherichia coli. A spontaneous IS30 insertion disrupting the type II restriction endonuclease gene notI increased plasmid transformation efficiency by about 2000-fold. Targeted deletion of notI reproduced this phenotype, confirming its role as a major barrier. Further deletion of the DNA phosphorothioation restriction locus dptFGH yielded an additional 10 to 37-fold improvement, generating the highly transformable ΔEPSΔFlgΔNotIΔPTRes chassis. Notably, the enhanced chassis further facilitated two linear-DNA-based editing strategies: direct RecET-mediated pyrF deletion using a linear donor coupled with phenotypic selection, achieving a recombination efficiency of 16.7%, and CRISPR/Cas9-assisted ribDHBA promoter replacement via co-delivery of a gRNA plasmid and a linear donor, achieving an efficiency of 11.1%. Together, these results identify endogenous restriction systems as primary barriers to genetic manipulation in H. bluephagenesis. Stepwise restriction release markedly improves plasmid transformation and enables linear DNA-mediated genome editing, providing an improved genetic platform for the iterative engineering of this industrial halophile. More broadly, this study suggests a practical strategy for overcoming the genetic inaccessibility of other non-model microorganisms and accelerating iterative strain engineering.

title: A background-suppressed CRISPR/Cas13a-HRCA biosensor for ultrasensitive miR-137 detection toward differential screening of Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Song J, Yue H, Zhang C, Jiao J, Jiao J
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is associated with pathological changes that can occur years before the onset of clinical symptoms, highlighting the importance of sensitive biomarker detection for early diagnosis. Here, we developed a fluorescence biosensing platform based on CRISPR/Cas13a-assisted hyperbranched rolling circle amplification (CRISPR/Cas13a-HRCA) for the detection of the AD-related biomarker miR-137. A duplex composed of Linear-Bio and a Cas13a linker strand was first immobilized on streptavidin-coated magnetic beads to construct magnetic probes. In the presence of miR-137, the linker strand was displaced and released into solution through strand exchange and magnetic separation. The released linker activated the CRISPR/Cas13a system via complementary pairing with crRNA, leading to cleavage of the UUU site within the topological DNA reporter (TDR). The cleaved TDR subsequently initiated the HRCA reaction in the presence of Vent DNA polymerase and the P2 probe, generating abundant double-stranded DNA products for fluorescence readout using SYBR Green I. By combining CRISPR/Cas13a amplification, magnetic separation, and label-free fluorescence detection, the platform produced a fluorescence response to miR-137 over 10 fM-100 nM, with an LOD and LOQ of 1.77 and 11.11 fM, respectively. Recoveries ranged from 99% to 106%, with RSDs of 2.2-2.6% in aCSF. Furthermore, the method successfully distinguished cerebrospinal fluid samples from AD patients and healthy individuals, demonstrating its potential for AD-related miRNA analysis.

title: De novo biosynthesis of meroterpenoid grifolic acid in Yarrowia lipolytica.
authors: Hong Y, Wang J, Wu Z, Lertphadungkit P, Yao R, Zhou B, Bar-Sela G, Cohen I
abstract: Grifolic acid, a potent bioactive meroterpenoid derived from fungi, shows great antitumor and antimicrobial properties. Nevertheless, the difficulty of large-scale chemical production and its minimal presence in natural environments hinder its path toward clinical translation. We developed a de novo grifolic acid biosynthetic route by leveraging the robust metabolic capabilities of the oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica. By improving the precursor malonyl-CoA supply through ACC1 overexpression and spatially targeting the fungal polyketide synthase ArmB to the vacuolar compartment, we enhanced orsellinic acid accumulation to 8.50 mg/L. We next leveraged AI-guided molecular docking and deep learning kinetic predictions (CataPro and UniKP) to screen candidate enzymes for coupling orsellinic acid with farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP), identifying StbC from Stachybotrys bisbyi as the optimal prenyltransferase for coupling the polyketide with the terpenoid moieties. Integrating the heterologous module with efflux pump engineering (overexpressing native Pleiotropic Drug Resistance ABC transporters) and blocking the competing β-oxidation pathway (through HBD1 deletion) relieved intracellular toxicity and minimized carbon loss. Under optimized conditions using a two-stage glucose-growth and glycerol-supplementation fed-batch regime, the engineered strain produced grifolic acid at 30.5 mg/L in a shaker flask. This work represents the first successful de novo production of grifolic acid in Y. lipolytica, validating a holistic metabolic engineering strategy for the sustainable synthesis of complex meroterpenoids.

title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing.
authors: Xing Y, Gao Y, Hong Z, Tian C, Cai H, Chu H, Yang Y, Liang PY
abstract: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. We operationally define 'benchmark-ready' organoid substrates using optional criteria encompassing viability, cellular identity, structural integrity, functional maturation, and baseline networks, supported by multimodal phenotyping. We further establish qualification metrics for organoid-machine interface and intrinsic neural and network function, including physical coupling, spatial coverage, temporal stability, spontaneous activity, and network-level organization. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical evaluation framework for stimulation-evoked computation combined with information encoding criteria, standardized scoring, and statistical reporting. We believe that the benchmarking framework may provide an adaptable foundation for standardized, reproducible and comparable evaluation of organoid computing technologies, thereby facilitating the broad adoption and application of organoid intelligence.

title: Enrichment characteristics and hyperspectral quantitative retrieval of lithium and rare earth element concentrations in coal.
authors: Zhao H, Cheng S, Wang M, Zhao L, Li C, Sun S, Wei Y, Tian Y
abstract: Coal is a host of critical metals, and rapid, non-destructive quantification of these metals is important for resource assessment. This study investigated lithium (Li) and rare earth elements (REE) in coal samples from the Sihe Coal Mine, Shanxi Province, and the Hebi Coal Mine, Henan Province, China. Hyperspectral data (350-2500 nm) were processed using First-order Derivative (FD) and Continuum Removal (CR), followed by feature selection with Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS) and Boruta. Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), Back-Propagation Neural Networks (BPNN), and Particle Swarm Optimization-Support Vector Regression (PSO-SVR) were used to develop quantitative retrieval models. Lithium was relatively enriched, whereas REE concentration were generally within the normal range. The FD-Boruta-BPNN model achieved the highest prediction accuracy for both Li (R2=0.912) and REE (R2=0.968), using fewer input wavelengths. These findings demonstrate that spectral preprocessing, feature selection, and modeling algorithms jointly influence retrieval performance, highlighting the need to balance predictive accuracy and model complexity. Predictions likely rely on indirect spectral information associated with mineral carriers rather than direct elemental absorption features. However, the limited sample size and geographical coverage constrain generalizability. Future research should incorporate larger, independent datasets from diverse geological settings, verify spectral-response mechanisms through mineralogical analysis, and extend the framework to other coal-hosted critical metals and hyperspectral imaging.

title: Multi-Loop Traction Device-Assisted Papillary Traction During Single-Balloon Enteroscopy-Assisted Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography After Roux-en-Y Gastrectomy: A Four-Case Series.
authors: Hirata D, Komoto S, Horiuchi T, Yoshioka M, Takahashi S, Furuhashi H, Narimatsu K, Hokari R
abstract: Biliary cannulation during single-balloon enteroscopy-assisted endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography after Roux-en-Y gastrectomy can remain challenging even after the papilla is reached. Unfavorable papillary orientation, tangential visualization, and excessive papillary mobility can impair alignment with the bile duct axis. We used a multi-loop traction device (MLTD; Boston Scientific Japan, Tokyo, Japan) as an adjunct for papillary traction in four patients with Roux-en-Y anatomy after gastrectomy. The indications were suspected distal bile duct cancer in one patient and common bile duct stones in three patients. An SIF-H290S enteroscope (Olympus Medical Systems Corp., Tokyo, Japan) was used in all patients. After MLTD traction, biliary cannulation and the intended diagnostic or therapeutic intervention were completed in all four cases. No procedure-related adverse events were observed during hospitalization or through the first outpatient visit after discharge. Traction corrected the papillary axis in papillae facing the blind limb and stabilized highly mobile papillae. MLTD-assisted papillary traction may serve as a practical rescue technique when difficult cannulation results from unfavorable papillary orientation or excessive mobility.

title: Simiao pill ameliorates collagen-induced arthritis in association with gut-joint axis modulation and attenuation of cGAS-STING signaling.
authors: Li T, Yang Y, Li G, Han L, Shen P, Ba X, Lin W, Yan J
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Simiao Pill formula (SM), composed of Phellodendron chinense C.K.Schneid., Atractylodes lancea (Thunb.) DC., Achyranthes bidentata Blume, and Coix lacryma-jobi var. ma-yuen (Rom.Caill.) Stapf, is a traditional Chinese herbal formula historically used for damp-heat Bi syndrome and commonly applied to the management of rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-related arthralgia symptoms. However, its anti-arthritic mechanisms remain incompletely defined. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study evaluated the anti-arthritic effects of SM in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) and examined whether these effects were associated with gut-joint axis-related alterations and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A CIA mouse model was established and treated with SM for 6 weeks. Arthritis severity, joint pathology, bone erosion, serum cytokines, lipopolysaccharide-binding protein, colonic histology, and tight junction proteins were assessed. Gut microbiota and colonic content metabolites were analyzed using 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. cGAS-STING pathway proteins were examined in joint and colonic tissues. A separate antibiotic-induced microbiota perturbation cohort was used to assess the contribution of gut microbiota to high-dose SM (SM-H) efficacy. RESULTS: SM reduced arthritis scores and spleen index in CIA mice. It decreased serum IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ levels, increased IL-10 production, and alleviated synovitis, cartilage damage, and bone erosion. SM also improved colonic histological abnormalities, enhanced colonic ZO-1 and Occludin expression, and reduced serum lipopolysaccharide-binding protein levels, suggesting improvement of intestinal barrier-related indicators. Gut microbiota and metabolomics analyses showed that SM-H reshaped gut microbial composition and colonic content metabolic profiles, particularly involving aromatic amino acid and vitamin-related metabolism. Correlation analysis linked representative microbial taxa and metabolites with arthritis severity, inflammatory responses, intestinal barrier markers, and bone parameters. Moreover, SM suppressed cGAS-STING pathway activation in both joint and colonic tissues. Under antibiotic exposure, the anti-arthritic, barrier-related, and cGAS-STING-inhibitory responses associated with SM-H were attenuated. CONCLUSIONS: SM ameliorated CIA in association with coordinated changes in gut microbial composition, colonic content metabolism, intestinal barrier-related indicators, systemic inflammation, and cGAS-STING signaling. Antibiotic exposure attenuated multiple SM-H-associated responses, supporting a contribution of microbiota-associated processes to the therapeutic response, although microbiota-specific causality was not established.

title: Siwu Paste alleviates blood deficiency syndrome induced by cyclophosphamide and acetylphenylhydrazine in association with gut microbiota remodeling and improved splenic metabolic homeostasis.
authors: Wan D, Feng X, Xu S, Du Q, Yue W, Zhang S
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Siwu Paste (SWP), derived from the classical blood-tonifying formula Siwu Decoction, has long been used for blood deficiency-related disorders and has a well-established traditional basis and ethnopharmacological value. Blood deficiency syndrome (BDS) is a common syndrome in traditional Chinese medicine and is associated with impaired blood generation and hematopoietic dysfunction. However, the modern pharmacological mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of SWP on BDS remain incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic effects of SWP on cyclophosphamide and acetylphenylhydrazine induced BDS and to investigate the potential mechanisms underlying its improvement of hematopoietic function. METHODS: The chemical constituents of SWP were characterized by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS), and its potential mechanisms were predicted using network pharmacology. An acetylphenylhydrazine (APH)/cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced BDS rat model was used to evaluate SWP efficacy through flow cytometry, histology, Western blotting, qPCR, 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and exogenous adenosine diphosphate (ADP) supplementation experiments were performed to evaluate the contribution of the gut microbiota and the involvement of splenic ADP-related metabolic alterations. RESULTS: SWP significantly improved hematopoietic dysfunction, alleviated systemic inflammation, restored intestinal barrier integrity, reversed the Treg/Th17 imbalance, and reduced apoptosis within the CD45+CD34+ bone marrow cell population in BDS rats. Multi-omics analysis revealed that SWP significantly regulated gut microbiota composition and metabolic profiles; specifically, SWP treatment was associated with a significant increase in the relative abundance of Allobaculum and an upward trend in Lactobacillus, accompanied by a significant reduction in the relative abundance of total ADP in spleen tissue compared with the BDS group. FMT experiments partially transferred the hematopoietic and immunomodulatory effects associated with SWP treatment. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment and exogenous ADP supplementation attenuated several SWP-induced improvements in bone-marrow hematopoietic function and Treg/Th17 balance, consistent with the involvement of the gut microbiota-splenic metabolic axis in the therapeutic effects of SWP. CONCLUSION: SWP alleviates bone marrow hematopoietic dysfunction in BDS rats, with these effects accompanied by gut microbiota remodeling, restoration of intestinal barrier integrity, suppression of inflammation, and improved metabolic homeostasis. These findings provide modern pharmacological evidence supporting the traditional TCM concept of "treating the marrow via the gut" in blood deficiency-related disorders.

title: Large prolapsed ureterocele with tissue necrosis presenting as vaginal bleeding and urinary retention in an adult woman: a case report.
authors: Warner A, Al-Karasneh A, Daggamseh A
abstract: Prolapse of a ureterocele through the urethra is rare in adults. A 55-year-old woman had unremarkable gynaecological investigation for postmenopausal bleeding. Two months later, after an Escherichia coli urinary tract infection, she re-presented with vaginal bleeding, an introital mass and urinary retention, initially attributed to pelvic organ prolapse. Urological assessment identified a left ureterocele prolapsing through the urethral meatus, which was reduced and appeared dusky. Computed tomography urography confirmed a single-system ureterocele. Endoscopic deroofing was performed, and histology showed prominent necrosis without malignancy. Prolapsed ureterocele should be considered in women with an introital mass, bleeding or retention.

title: Aberrant Artery Contributing to Thoracic Outlet Syndrome.
authors: Tan L, Gehrmann E, Radwan T, Tan V
journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
abstract: Thoracic outlet syndrome results from the compression of neurovascular structures as they pass through the thoracic outlet, often leading to neurogenic symptoms involving the brachial plexus. We present two cases of young adults with persistent upper arm and hand symptoms due to brachial plexus compression associated with aberrant arteries. Despite nonsurgical management, including physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medications, both patients continued to experience disabling symptoms. Surgical exploration has revealed previously undescribed anomalous arterial branches deep to the anterior scalene muscle and crossing directly over the C7-T1 nerve roots. These arteries were ligated and divided, in addition to brachial plexus neurolysis and scalenectomies. Both patients experienced complete resolution of symptoms postoperatively and returned to full activity. Given that the vascular anomaly was addressed alongside standard decompression procedures, its independent contribution to symptom relief cannot be fully established. However, the direct relationship between the aberrant artery and compressed nerve roots suggests it remains a contributing factor. These cases highlight the importance of considering rare vascular anomalies as potential contributors to neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome, particularly in the young adult population. Recognition of such variants is critical during surgical dissection, as standard imaging may not identify these atypical compressive structures.

title: Modular engineering of aromatic metabolism in Corynebacterium glutamicum enables protocatechuic acid and gallic acid production.
authors: Pei J, Huang Q, Zhang B, Chu X, Wu X, Guo X, Ye B, Zhang B
abstract: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) and gallic acid (GA) are valuable phenolic compounds with diverse pharmacological activities, including antioxidant and antitumor properties, and have broad applications in the food, cosmetic, chemical, and pharmaceutical industries. However, the industrial production of these compounds remains limited by the insufficient performance of current microbial cell factories, resulting in low productivity and high manufacturing costs. Here, an efficient biosynthetic platform based on Corynebacterium glutamicum was systematically established for the production of PCA and GA. Through reconstruction of the PCA biosynthetic pathway, elimination of competing branches in the shikimate pathway, enhancement of the key rate-limiting enzyme, and modulation of the glucose uptake system to increase phosphoenolpyruvate supply, metabolic flux was effectively redirected toward PCA accumulation, resulting in the engineered strain PCA16 achieving a PCA titer of 19.8 g/L in shake-flask fermentation. Building on this platform, GA biosynthesis was established by introducing a mutant pobA from Pseudomonas aeruginosa and further strengthening the shikimate pathway, enabling strain GA06 to produce 7.86 g/L GA in shake-flask fermentation. Upon scale-up in a 5 L bioreactor, GA production was further increased to 25.66 g/L, representing the highest reported titer for GA production using C. glutamicum to date. Overall, this work demonstrates the strong potential of C. glutamicum as a robust microbial chassis for efficient production of PCA and GA, and provides a versatile platform for the biosynthesis of PCA-derived aromatic compounds.

title: Engineered microorganisms drive local metabolic reprogramming to Re-educate systemic immunity.
authors: Ma Y, Yang Y, Yu Z, Jin M, Jin Y, Wang J, Wang H, Zhao Q
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) features chronic synovial inflammation and systemic immune disorders. Current treatments mainly rely on systemic immunosuppression, raising risks of infection and long-term immune injury. Local therapies reduce such risks but struggle to regulate systemic immunity. Emerging studies show the synovial immunometabolic microenvironment links local inflammation to systemic responses. Here, we developed a strategy based on chemically attenuated photosynthetic bacteria that couples lactate metabolism with photo-driven hydrogen production to achieve local metabolic reprogramming and systemic immune re-education. We screened a photosynthetic bacterial strain with high lactate metabolic capacity, which also exhibited enhanced hydrogen production. To ensure safety, bacteria were PEGylated to mask immunogenic moieties while preserving metabolic activity. Intra-articular injection disrupted pathological crosstalk and restored the Treg/Th17 balance locally. Circulating IL-6 levels decreased, restoring the systemic regulatory role of Tregs, thereby alleviating distant joint inflammation. These results demonstrate that local synovial metabolic reprogramming by engineered bacteria can induce systemic immune re-education, offering a conceptually new therapeutic strategy for treating autoimmune arthritis.

title: Dual-zone swelling microneedle-smartphone platform for simultaneous colorimetric quantification of glucose and pH in diabetic wound interstitial fluid.
authors: Zhou Y, Li S, He L, Qi L, Yin G, Zhou H, Long W, Chen Y
abstract: Diabetic wounds undergo dynamic changes in local metabolism and infection-associated microenvironments, making timely assessment of wound status challenging. Herein, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first dual-zone swelling microneedle-smartphone platform for simultaneous colorimetric quantification of glucose and pH directly from diabetic wound interstitial fluid (ISF). The platform combines a swelling microneedle patch, termed "IDB-CMN", with a companion WeChat mini program, "IDB-CMN Insight". Two spatially separated response zones are incorporated into the patch, using a glucose oxidase-horseradish peroxidase-3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (GOx-HRP-TMB) cascade for glucose detection and m-cresol purple (mCP) for pH sensing. After local ISF uptake, the resulting colorimetric responses are analyzed by IDB-CMN Insight, which extracts RGB values from user-selected regions and converts them into quantitative glucose concentrations and pH values using pre-established calibration equations. The patch exhibited a mechanical strength of approximately 0.4 N per needle and a maximum swelling ratio of approximately 305%, with quantitative response ranges of 0.5-5.0 mg mL-1 for glucose and pH 6.0-10.0. In non-infected and Staphylococcus aureus-infected diabetic mouse wounds, the platform captured temporal changes in local glucose and pH that were consistent with conventional measurements, while infected wounds maintained a more alkaline microenvironment. Concurrent analysis of these two parameters provides complementary information on local metabolic and infection-associated changes and may offer early indications of adverse microenvironmental shifts during wound healing, supporting future risk assessment and treatment optimization.
